title: Phnom Penh International Half Marathon 2027 Review: Starting at a 15th-Century Pagoda
seo_title: Phnom Penh International Half Marathon 2027 Review
meta_description: Phnom Penh International Half Marathon 2027 review: June 13 at Wat Botum Park -- next to one of Cambodia's oldest pagodas, founded in the 15th century.
dek: Set for 13 June 2027 at Botumvatey Pagoda Park (Wat Botum Park), this race starts beside one of the five oldest pagodas in Phnom Penh, founded by King Ponhea Yat in the 15th century.
verdict: The Phnom Penh International Half Marathon starts at Wat Botum Park, adjacent to Wat Botum Vathey -- one of the five oldest pagodas in Phnom Penh, founded by King Ponhea Yat in the 15th century, south of the Royal Palace. The park itself hosts the Cambodia-Vietnam Friendship Monument, giving the course genuine historical and diplomatic significance. Three distances (5K/10K/21K) with registration already open, organised by Cambodia Events, make this a straightforward, culturally rich pick in a country otherwise underrepresented in this research batch.

sections.heading: Starting Beside a 15th-Century Pagoda
paragraphs: The race offers three distances -- 5K, 10K and 21K -- starting at Botumvatey Pagoda Park (Wat Botum Park) in Phnom Penh, organised by Cambodia Events. [1] Wat Botum is a Khmer Buddhist pagoda built by King Ponhea Yat (1405-1467) in the 15th century, located south of the Royal Palace of Cambodia -- one of the five oldest pagodas in the city, with ancient origins. [2]

sections.heading: A Park With Diplomatic Significance
paragraphs: Wat Botum Park is a large open space with fountains, benches and a children's playground, lying east of the pagoda. [2] Its centrepiece is the Cambodia-Vietnam Friendship Monument, a Soviet-style sculpture commemorating the alliance between the two nations and the liberation of Phnom Penh from the Khmer Rouge -- giving this course genuine 20th-century political and historical weight alongside its 15th-century religious heritage.

sections.heading: A Rare Cambodia Entry
paragraphs: Cambodia is significantly underrepresented in this research batch compared to Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines, making this genuinely one of the few Cambodian races covered -- similar in rarity to the Yoma Yangon International Marathon's Myanmar coverage elsewhere in this research.

sections.heading: Registration Already Open
paragraphs: Registration is currently open across all three distances. [1] Combined with the race's genuine historical setting, this makes it one of the more straightforward, culturally rich picks in this final batch of the research.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a half marathon starting beside one of Phnom Penh's oldest and most historically significant pagodas -- in a country rarely covered by regional race calendars -- the Phnom Penh International Half Marathon on 13 June 2027 is a genuinely compelling pick. Registration is already open.
